Subject: Private deployment — evidence access and operator runbook

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward a pilot PO but Legal raised a few specific asks on private/on‑prem deployments that we need addressed in the MSA/Order Form addendum before procurement can sign:

1) Forensic snapshot access — we need an auditable mechanism for a mutually agreed custodian to obtain a point‑in‑time snapshot (logs + model binary + runbook) in the event of termination or suspected compromise.
2) Operator runbook embargo — we require a redacted operator runbook during normal ops, but an unredacted runbook available under defined escalation triggers.
3) Audit triggers — procurement wants a clear set of triggers (SLA breaches, security incident, regulatory request) and a maximum SLA for access delivery (we proposed 10 business days).

I've attached our Audit_Timeline and a draft PO that outlines the pilot milestones. Can Redwood provide suggested language for an addendum and a short list of custody/transfer options (escrow, third‑party custodian, remote witness certification)?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement has a target of end of month for the pilot PO.

Thanks,
Sarah Lee
Head of IT Security 
MedTech Solutions
attachments: MedTech_Audit_Timeline.pdf, PO_pending.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — evidence access and operator runbook

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Good news: we have a couple of patterns customers use depending on risk profile. High level options we can propose for the addendum:

A) Escrow + warden access (custodian escrow): vendor deposits a snapshot and encrypted key with a neutral escrow agent; release conditions defined in addendum; custody handoff supervised by both parties.
B) Remote witness + ephemeral transfer: Redwood performs an encrypted snapshot and transfers under a remote witness protocol (video & hash verification) to customer or custodian; suitable for small pilots.
C) Scripted operator runbook gating: runbook redaction policy with an escalation matrix that provisions full runbook within X business days when a trigger is met.

Proposal for timeline: we can commit to delivering snapshot access under trigger conditions within 10 business days for escrow + supervised transfer, and 3 business days for remote witness for most incident types. For legal, we'll provide proposed language for: scope of snapshot (logs + model artifacts + config), verification hashes, key custody, redaction rules for PII/source code, and mutual non‑destructive verification steps.

Looping in Priyom from Legal to draft the addendum language and advise on any regulatory carveouts. Is 10 business days acceptable as your procurement suggested upper bound? Also — are there any regulatory data residency constraints we should be aware of?

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sarah / Neha — thanks for the summary. Below is draft clause language we can include in an MSA addendum (we've kept it tight to minimize review cycles):

--- DRAFT ADDENDUM LANGUAGE (for negotiation) ---
1) Snapshot & Custody: Upon a Trigger Event (defined below), Redwood will produce a time‑stamped, immutable snapshot consisting of: system logs (last 90 days), model artifacts (deployed model binary and associated weights), and deployment configuration. Redwood will provide a cryptographic hash of the snapshot and either (a) deposit the snapshot encrypted with a key escrowed with [Neutral Custodian], or (b) transfer the snapshot to Customer under a Remote Witness protocol.

2) Trigger Events: Trigger Events include (i) material SLA failure lasting > 72 hours, (ii) substantiated security incident impacting confidentiality/integrity, (iii) lawful regulatory request or court order, or (iv) termination without cure where Customer has paid for dedicated capacity within the prior 12 months.

3) Delivery SLA: For escrow deposit + release, Redwood will effect deposit and release procedures within 10 business days of validated Trigger Event. For Remote Witness transfers, Redwood will complete transfer within 3 business days of validated Trigger Event, subject to mutual availability.

4) Runbook Redaction & Access: Redwood will maintain an Operator Runbook in redacted form for normal operations. Upon a Trigger Event, Redwood will provide an unredacted runbook under an access agreement for forensic review, subject to standard NDAs and controls; access will be provided within the Delivery SLA above.

5) Verification & Non‑Destructive Access: All transfer steps will include cryptographic verification and a joint checklist to ensure non‑destructive validation.

6) Fees & Escrow Costs: Customer will reimburse reasonable third‑party custodian fees and any incremental transfer costs; otherwise no additional fees for snapshot creation.

--- end draft ---

Questions for MedTech: is the 90‑day log window sufficient? Do you need longer retention in the snapshot? Also confirm whether any of the Trigger Events should be tightened/loosened.

Marissa — please review clause 6 (fees) for our standard procurement response; we should be consistent with other on‑prem pilots.

Best,
Priyom Das
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom and Neha — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick responses:

• 90 days logs is OK for the pilot; long‑term we may ask for 12 months in production, but that's out of scope for the pilot PO.
• Trigger Events: procurement asked to clarify whether "termination without cure" requires a prior notice window. We prefer: termination without cure after 30 days' written notice.
• Delivery SLA: 10 business days for escrow is acceptable. For Remote Witness, can you confirm we get a downloadable copy (not just access) once transfer completes?

We have attached two files: MedTech_Audit_Timeline.pdf (shows milestones) and the draft PO. Procurement's target signature date is 2026‑11‑05.

Next actions agreed:
1) Redwood Legal to update the draft addendum to add the 30‑day notice clarification and explicit confirmation that Remote Witness results in a downloadable copy for Customer (subject to verification).
2) Redwood to estimate any third‑party custodian fees for the escrow option (ballpark).
3) Neha to share an internal runbook redaction checklist so MedTech can preview what is redacted vs what will be provided after a Trigger Event.

If you can get the draft addendum to us by COB Monday (2026‑11‑01) procurement will push the PO forward.

Appreciate the quick response.
